Bấm để máy tự động đọc lần lượt từng từ và hiển thị theo dõi (phù hợp học trên điện thoại)
1. journalism (n)
/ˈdʒɜːnəlɪzəm/
ngành báo chí, nghề làm báo (n: journalist — nhà báo)
Collocation: investigative journalism, ethical journalism, citizen journalism
"Investigative journalism plays a vital role in exposing corruption and holding leaders accountable."
2. broadcast (v/n)
/ˈbrɔːdkɑːst/
phát sóng (truyền hình, phát thanh); chương trình phát sóng (quá khứ/phân từ giữ nguyên: broadcast)
Collocation: broadcast live, national television broadcast, news broadcast
"The Prime Minister's speech was broadcast live on national television and radio."
3. coverage (n)
/ˈkʌvərɪdʒ/
sự đưa tin, thời lượng/mức độ phủ sóng tin tức về một sự kiện (không đếm được)
Collocation: extensive media coverage, biased coverage, live coverage
"The Olympic Games received extensive media coverage across television and digital platforms."
4. bias (n/v)
/ˈbaɪəs/
sự thiên vị, định kiến một chiều (adj: biased — thiên vị, thiếu khách quan)
Collocation: political bias, media bias, free from bias, biased reporting
"Readers should compare multiple news sources to avoid being misled by political bias."
5. objective (adj)
/əbˈdʒektɪv/
khách quan, trung thực dựa trên sự thật (trái nghĩa: subjective — chủ quan)
Collocation: objective reporting, remain objective, objective analysis
"Professional journalists must remain objective and present both sides of a controversy fairly."
6. sensational (adj)
/senˈseɪʃənl/
giật gân, câu khách (n: sensationalism — chủ nghĩa báo chí giật gân câu view)
Collocation: sensational headlines, sensationalist tabloid news
"Tabloid newspapers often use sensational headlines about celebrity scandals to boost clicks."
7. verify (v)
/ˈverɪfaɪ/
xác minh, kiểm chứng độ chính xác của thông tin (n: verification)
Collocation: verify the facts, verify the authenticity of a source
"Responsible citizens always verify breaking news on reputable websites before sharing it online."
8. distort (v)
/dɪˈstɔːt/
bóp méo, xuyên tạc sự thật
Collocation: distort the truth, distort facts, grossly distorted
"Social media rumours can easily distort the truth and cause unnecessary public panic."
9. exaggerate (v)
/ɪɡˈzædʒəreɪt/
phóng đại, thổi phồng quá mức (n: exaggeration)
Collocation: exaggerate the danger, wildly exaggerated claims
"Some online influencers exaggerate the benefits of diet pills to earn advertising money."
10. credibility (n)
/ˌkredəˈbɪləti/
độ tin cậy, uy tín (adj: credible — đáng tin cậy)
Collocation: lose credibility, high credibility, credible news source
"Once a newspaper publishes fabricated stories, it permanently damages its public credibility."
11. paparazzi (n)
/ˌpæpəˈrætsi/
thợ săn ảnh đeo bám người nổi tiếng (danh từ số nhiều)
Collocation: intrusive paparazzi, hounded by paparazzi
"Strict privacy laws are needed to stop intrusive paparazzi from harassing celebrities' children."
12. editorial (n/adj)
/ˌedɪˈtɔːriəl/
bài xã luận; thuộc về ban biên tập báo chí
Collocation: editorial standards, newspaper editorial, editorial independence
"Unlike random social media blogs, traditional newspapers adhere to strict editorial standards."
13. algorithm (n)
/ˈælɡərɪðəm/
thuật toán (máy tính/mạng xã hội tự động đề xuất nội dung)
Collocation: social media algorithms, recommendation algorithm
"Social media algorithms are designed to maximize user engagement by promoting controversial posts."
14. disinformation (n)
/ˌdɪsɪnfəˈmeɪʃn/
thông tin sai lệch có chủ đích (tin giả được tung ra để lừa dối dư luận)
Collocation: spread disinformation, combat online disinformation
"Schools must teach media literacy so students can recognize online disinformation and fake news."
15. transparent (adj)
/trænsˈpærənt/
minh bạch, rõ ràng không giấu giếm (n: transparency)
Collocation: transparent reporting, government transparency
"Public trust increases when media organizations are transparent about how they fund their stories."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Động Từ Tường Thuật Học Thuật (Academic Reporting Verbs) & Giới Từ Đi Kèm

• Thay vì lặp đi lặp lại say / think trong Writing Task 2, hãy sử dụng các cấu trúc động từ tường thuật chủ đề Truyền thông:
  1. accuse + Object + of + V-ing (Cáo buộc ai làm gì):
    Ví dụ: Critics often accuse tabloid newspapers of exaggerating minor scandals to boost sales.
  2. blame + Object + for + V-ing / Noun (Đổ lỗi cho ai về việc gì):
    Ví dụ: Sociologists blame social media algorithms for spreading disinformation.
  3. claim / allege / maintain + that + S + V (Tuyên bố / Cáo buộc / Khẳng định rằng):
    Ví dụ: Proponents of citizen journalism maintain that smartphones allow ordinary people to expose injustice.

🔵 Tầng 2: Cấu Trúc Bị Động Tường Thuật (Passive Reporting Structures) — C1 Academic Style

• Công thức 1 (Chủ ngữ giả It): It is widely reported / alleged / claimed that + S + V
  Ví dụ: It is widely reported that sensational headlines attract three times more clicks than objective news.

• Công thức 2 (Đưa Chủ ngữ lên đầu + to-V): S + is / are + often accused of / reported to + V
  Ví dụ: Intrusive paparazzi are often accused of invading the private lives of public figures.
   Lưu ý: Động từ broadcast giữ nguyên hình thái ở cả 3 cột (broadcast - broadcast - broadcast): The debate was broadcast live yesterday.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. Investigative ________ is essential in a democracy because it exposes political corruption and corporate fraud.
2. The championship football match was ________ live to over two hundred million viewers worldwide.
3. Environmental disasters often receive far less media ________ than celebrity weddings and divorces.
4. A reputable news channel must report the facts fairly without showing any political or commercial ________.
5. Good reporters strive to remain ________ by interviewing experts from both sides of a debate.
6. Tabloid websites frequently use ________ clickbait headlines to shock readers and increase advertising revenue.
7. Professional editors always ________ the accuracy of statistics and quotes before publishing an article.
8. Taking a politician's words out of context can completely ________ the original meaning of their speech.
9. Unethical bloggers often ________ minor health risks to frighten readers into buying their products.
10. Traditional print newspapers enjoy higher public ________ than anonymous social media accounts.
11. Aggressive ________ waited outside the hospital with telephoto cameras to take photos of the actress.
12. Every article in our magazine must pass strict ________ fact-checking by senior editors.
13. Video apps use a complex recommendation ________ to keep teenagers scrolling for hours.
14. During election campaigns, foreign hackers sometimes use fake accounts to spread ________ and confuse voters.
15. Democratic governments must be open and ________ about how public tax money is spent.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 22] Public art galleries and classical literature ________ our spiritual lives and foster creativity.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 21] As the population ages, a shrinking ________ must support a growing number of retirees.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 20] Untreated chemical waste from factories can ________ local drinking water reservoirs.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 18] Farmers use natural compost and crop rotation in ________ agriculture to protect soil fertility.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 15] Citizens who fail to verify emails may fall ________ to online banking cybercrime.
Điểm: 0/20

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Media critics often accuse tabloid newspapers ________ sensational headlines to attract clicks.
2. Psychologists blame social media algorithms ________ teenagers' declining attention spans.
3. Note the irregular past participle of 'broadcast': The emergency weather warning ________ live across all channels last night.
4. Note that 'news' and 'coverage' are uncountable: Extensive media coverage ________ given to the climate summit yesterday.
5. ________ is widely reported that fake news spreads six times faster on social media than verified facts.
6. Intrusive paparazzi are frequently accused of ________ the privacy of celebrities and their children.
7. ________ the high speed of social media news, many unverified rumours lack credibility.
8. Before ________ breaking news on social networks, responsible internet users always verify the source.
9. Unless social media platforms regulate disinformation, public trust in journalism ________ to decline.
10. By 2030, digital news subscriptions are projected ________ print newspaper sales in every age segment.
Điểm: 0/10

👩 Editor-in-Chief: Good morning, University Media and Journalism Society, Editor Rachel Green speaking. How can I help you?
👨 First-Year Student: Hello Rachel! My name is Daniel Kowalski. I am a first-year communications student, and I would love to join the campus newspaper team.
👩 Editor-in-Chief: Welcome, Daniel! We are always looking for passionate student reporters. Could you spell your surname for our press badge form?
👨 First-Year Student: Yes, it is Kowalski. K - O - W - A - L - S - K - I. 💡 Đáp án câu 1 (Họ phóng viên sinh viên): KOWALSKI
👩 Editor-in-Chief: Thank you. Which section of our newspaper are you most interested in writing for?
👨 First-Year Student: I used to write sports reviews in high school, but now I want to focus on Science and Technology coverage. 💡 Bẫy quá khứ (sports) vs hiện tại câu 2: Science / Technology
👩 Editor-in-Chief: That is great! Because there is so much online disinformation today, all new writers must attend our mandatory training workshop on Fact Verification. 💡 Đáp án câu 3 (Chủ đề workshop bắt buộc): Fact Verification / Verification
👨 First-Year Student: I completely agree—objective reporting and credibility are vital. When does the editorial team meet each week?
👩 Editor-in-Chief: Our weekly editorial meeting takes place every Tuesday evening at 5:30 PM. 💡 Đáp án câu 4 (Ngày họp biên tập hàng tuần): Tuesday
👨 First-Year Student: How many words should my first trial article be?
👩 Editor-in-Chief: Feature stories are usually 800 words, but for your first trial report, please write 450 words. 💡 Bẫy độ dài bài thường (800) vs bài thử việc đầu tiên câu 5: 450
👨 First-Year Student: Four hundred and fifty words is very manageable. Does the society also produce a weekly radio broadcast?
👩 Editor-in-Chief: Yes! We broadcast a live campus news podcast every Friday from Studio B in the Media Centre. 💡 Đáp án câu 6 (Địa điểm phòng thu): Media Centre
👨 First-Year Student: Can I bring my laptop and camera to the Tuesday meeting?
👩 Editor-in-Chief: Of course! We will issue your student press pass on Tuesday at 5:30 PM. See you then!

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - The Rise of Citizen Journalism and Instant Coverage]
Over the past two decades, the rise of smartphones and social networks has revolutionized how news is produced and consumed. Previously, the public relied on television broadcasts and print newspapers, which were regulated by professional editorial boards. Today, anyone with an internet connection can publish breaking news instantly, providing live coverage of global events and exposing social injustice without government censorship.

[Paragraph B - Algorithms, Sensationalism and the Spread of Disinformation]
However, this digital shift has severely undermined the credibility of modern journalism. Because social media platforms rely on advertising revenue, their recommendation algorithms prioritize posts that provoke anger or shock rather than objective analysis. Consequently, unethical websites publish sensational clickbait headlines, exaggerate minor conflicts, and distort scientific facts. Worse still, malicious groups exploit these platforms to spread political disinformation, while users are trapped in 'echo chambers' that reinforce their existing bias.

[Paragraph C - Restoring Public Trust Through Verification and Transparency]
To restore public trust in the media, action is required from both news organizations and citizens. Media outlets must uphold transparent editorial standards, employ independent fact-checkers to verify every source, and respect privacy laws rather than hiring intrusive paparazzi. Simultaneously, schools should integrate media literacy into the curriculum so that young people learn to cross-check information and distinguish credible journalism from online falsehoods.
Điểm: 0/6
